title.zh: 卷一百〇七 志第六十 禮十
title.raw: 卷一百〇七 志第六十 禮十 Volume 107 Treatises 60: Rites 10

sentences.zh: 宗廟之禮。

translations.literal: Rites of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Rites of the Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 每歲以四孟月及季冬，凡五享，朔、望則上食、薦新。

translations.literal: Each year, in the four first months of the seasons and the last month of winter, there were five offerings in all; on the new and full moons, food was presented and new harvests were offered.
translations.idiomatic: Each year there were five regular offerings, held in the first month of each season and in the last month of winter; on the new and full moons, additional food offerings and presentations of the new harvest were made.

sentences.zh: 三年一祫，以孟冬；

translations.literal: Once every three years there was a xiá offering, held in the first month of winter;
translations.idiomatic: A great xiá merging sacrifice was held once every three years, in the first month of winter;

sentences.zh: 五年一禘，以孟夏，唯親郊、封祀。

translations.literal: once every five years there was a dì offering, held in the first month of summer—except when the emperor personally performed suburban or feng sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: and a great dì sacrifice once every five years, in the first month of summer—unless the emperor was personally conducting suburban rites or a fengshan ceremony.

sentences.zh: 又有朝享、告謝及新主祔謁，皆大祀也。

translations.literal: There were also morning offerings, thanksgiving rites, and visits when a new spirit tablet was enshrined—all major sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Morning offerings, thanksgiving ceremonies, and rites when a new ancestral tablet was installed were also counted among the major sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二薦，則行一獻禮。

translations.literal: For the two seasonal presentations, a single-offering rite was performed.
translations.idiomatic: For the two seasonal presentation offerings, a simplified single-presentation rite was used.

sentences.zh: 其祔祭，春祀司命及戶，夏祀灶，季夏祀中霤，秋祀門及厲，冬祀行，惟臘享、禘祫則遍祀焉。

translations.literal: For the associated sacrifices: in spring, the Director of Fate and the Door were worshiped; in summer, the Stove; in the last month of summer, the Central Drain; in autumn, the Gate and the Pestilence Spirit; in winter, the Path—only at the la offering and at the dì and xiá rites were all of them worshiped together.
translations.idiomatic: Associated household spirits received seasonal worship: the Director of Fate and the Door in spring, the Stove in summer, the Central Drain in the last month of summer, the Gate and the Pestilence Spirit in autumn, and the Path in winter; only at the year-end la offering and at the great dì and xiá ceremonies were they all worshiped together.

sentences.zh: 禘祫之禮。

translations.literal: Rites of the dì and xiá offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Rites of the Dì and Xiá Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平二年八月，太常禮院言：「今年冬祭畫日，以十月六日薦享太廟。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Xianping under Emperor Zhenzong, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in the Ministry of Rites reported: "The winter sacrifice for this year has been scheduled; the presentation offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple is set for the sixth day of the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of the Xianping era, Emperor Zhenzong's Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "The winter sacrifice has been scheduled for this year, with a presentation offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple on the sixth day of the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 按《禮》，三年一祫，以孟冬。

translations.literal: According to the Rites, there is a xiá offering once every three years, held in the first month of winter.
translations.idiomatic: According to the canonical Rites, a xiá merging sacrifice should be held once every three years, in the first month of winter.

sentences.zh: 又《疑義》云：三年喪畢，遭禘則禘，遭袷 則袷。

translations.literal: The Doubts on the Rites also states: when the three-year mourning is complete, if a dì offering falls due, perform the dì; if a xiá falls due, perform the xiá.
translations.idiomatic: The Doubts on the Rites further states that when the three-year mourning period ends, whichever great sacrifice comes due first should be performed—dì if a dì is due, xiá if a xiá is due.

sentences.zh: 宜改孟冬薦享為祫享。」

translations.literal: The first-month-of-winter presentation offering should be changed to a xiá offering."
translations.idiomatic: The winter presentation offering should therefore be changed to a xiá merging sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖元年，禮官言：「真宗神主祔廟，已行吉祭，三年之制，又從易月之文，自天禧二年四月禘享，至今已及五年，合行禘禮。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiansheng under Emperor Renzong, the ritual officials reported: "Emperor Zhenzong's spirit tablet has been enshrined in the temple and the auspicious sacrifice has been performed. The three-year rule, following the text on abbreviated mourning, has been observed. Since the dì offering in the fourth month of the second year of Tianxi, five years have now passed—it is time to perform the dì rite."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tiansheng era, ritual officials reported: "Now that Emperor Zhenzong's spirit tablet has been installed in the ancestral temple and the auspicious installation sacrifice completed, and with the three-year mourning period observed according to the abbreviated mourning rule, five full years have passed since the dì sacrifice of the fourth month, second year of Tianxi. It is time to perform the dì rite again.

sentences.zh: 遂以孟夏薦享為禘享。

translations.literal: Accordingly, the first-month-of-summer presentation offering was made a dì offering.
translations.idiomatic: The first-month-of-summer presentation offering was accordingly conducted as a dì sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 八年九月，太常禮院言：「自天聖六年夏行禘享之禮，至此年十月，請以孟冬薦享為祫享。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Since the dì offering was performed in the summer of the sixth year of Tiansheng, by the tenth month of this year it is requested that the first-month-of-winter presentation offering be made a xiá offering."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Since the dì sacrifice was performed in the summer of the sixth year of Tiansheng, the winter presentation offering scheduled for the tenth month of this year should be conducted as a xiá merging sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 詔恭依。

translations.literal: An edict directed that this be respectfully followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐四年十月，仁宗親 詣太廟行祫享禮，以宰臣富弼為祫享大禮使，韓琦為禮儀使，樞密使宋庠為儀仗使，參知政事曾公亮為橋道頓遞使，樞密副使程戡為鹵簿使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Jiayou, Emperor Renzong personally went to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to perform the xiá offering. Fu Bi, a chief councilor, was appointed Grandee of the Xiá Offering; Han Qi, Master of Ceremonies; Song Qi, Commissioner of the Privy Council, Master of Insignia; Zeng Gongliang, Vice Grand Councilor, Master of Bridge Roads and Relay Stations; and Cheng Kan, Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, Master of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Jiayou, Emperor Renzong went in person to the Imperial Ancestral Temple to perform the xiá merging sacrifice. Chief Councilor Fu Bi served as Grandee of the Xiá Rite; Han Qi as Master of Ceremonies; Privy Council Commissioner Song Qi as Master of Insignia; Vice Grand Councilor Zeng Gongliang as Master of Bridge Roads and Relay Arrangements; and Vice Privy Council Commissioner Cheng Kan as Master of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 同判宗正寺趙良規請正 太祖東向位，禮官不敢決。

translations.literal: Zhao Lianggui, Associate Administrator of the Court of the Imperial Clan, requested that Taizu be given the correct east-facing position, but the ritual officials did not dare decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lianggui, associate administrator of the Court of the Imperial Clan, petitioned to rectify Taizu's east-facing seat, but the ritual officials declined to rule on the matter.

sentences.zh: 觀文殿學士王舉正等議曰：「大祫之禮所以合昭穆，辨尊卑，必以受命之祖居東向之位。

translations.literal: Wang Juzheng, Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, and others deliberated: "The great xiá rite serves to unite the zhao and mu lines and distinguish superior from inferior; the ancestor who received the Mandate must occupy the east-facing position.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Wang Juzheng of the Hall for Viewing Literature and his colleagues argued: "The great xiá sacrifice exists to unite the zhao and mu ancestral lines and to distinguish rank; the founder who received the Mandate must occupy the east-facing seat.

sentences.zh: 本朝以太祖為受命之君，然僖祖以降，四廟在 上，故每遇大袷，止列昭穆而虛東向。

translations.literal: Our dynasty takes Taizu as the ruler who received the Mandate, yet from Emperor Xi onward four ancestral temples stand above him; therefore at each great xiá only the zhao and mu are arrayed while the east-facing seat is left vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty recognizes Taizu as the ruler who received the Mandate, but with four ancestral temples above him from Emperor Xi onward, at each great xiá only the zhao and mu tablets are arranged while the east-facing seat is left vacant.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，亦用此禮。

translations.literal: Since the Wei and Jin dynasties, this rite has also been used.
translations.idiomatic: The same practice has been followed since the Wei and Jin periods.

sentences.zh: 今親享之盛，宜如舊便。」

translations.literal: For this grand occasion of personal attendance, it is fitting to follow the old practice."
translations.idiomatic: For this solemn occasion of the emperor's personal attendance, the established practice should be maintained."

sentences.zh: 禮官張洞、韓維言：「國朝每遇禘祫，奉別廟四後之主合食 太廟。

translations.literal: The ritual officials Zhang Dong and Han Wei stated: "Whenever our dynasty performs the dì or xiá offerings, the spirit tablets of the four empresses from the separate temples are brought to share the feast at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials Zhang Dong and Han Wei argued: "At each dì and xiá sacrifice, our dynasty brings the spirit tablets of the four empresses from their separate temples to share the communal feast in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 唐《郊祀志》載禘祫祝文，自獻祖至肅宗所配皆一後，惟睿宗二後，蓋昭成，明皇母也。

translations.literal: The Tang Record of Suburban Sacrifices records the prayer texts for dì and xiá offerings: from Emperor Xianzu through Emperor Suzong, each was paired with a single empress—only Emperor Ruizong had two empresses, namely Zhaocheng, mother of Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Record of Suburban Sacrifices lists the prayer texts for dì and xiá sacrifices: from Emperor Xianzu through Emperor Suzong, each emperor was paired with only one empress—Emperor Ruizong alone had two, Zhaocheng being the mother of Emperor Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 《續曲台禮》有別廟皇后合食之文，蓋未有本室，遇祫享即祔祖姑 下。

translations.literal: The Continued Rites of the Qu Terrace contains passages on empresses from separate temples sharing the feast—because they had no shrine of their own, when a xiá offering occurred they were enshrined below the founding ancestress.
translations.idiomatic: The Continued Rites of the Qu Terrace includes provisions for empresses of separate temples to share the communal feast—when they lacked their own shrine, they were placed below the founding ancestress at the xiá sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 所以大順中，三太后配列禘祭，議者議其非禮。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Dazhun era, when three empress dowagers were ranked together in the dì sacrifice, deliberators criticized this as contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When three empress dowagers were ranked together in a dì sacrifice during the Dazhun era, critics condemned the practice as improper.

sentences.zh: 臣謂每室既有定配，則餘後不當參列，義當革正。」

translations.literal: Your subjects hold that since each shrine already has its fixed pairing, the remaining empresses ought not to be included in the array—it is right to correct this."
translations.idiomatic: We hold that since each imperial shrine already has its designated consort, additional empresses should not be included in the array, and the practice ought to be corrected."

sentences.zh: 學士孫抃等議：「《春秋傳》曰：『大祫者 何，合祭也。

translations.literal: Academician Sun Bian and others deliberated: "The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals states: 'What is the great xiá? It is a combined sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Sun Bian and his colleagues countered: "The Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals asks, 'What is the great xiá?' and answers, 'A combined sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 未毀廟之主皆升合食於太祖。』

translations.literal: The tablets of all shrines not yet dismantled ascend to share the feast with Taizu.'
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablets of all shrines not yet dismantled ascend to share the feast with Taizu.'

sentences.zh: 是以國朝事宗廟百有餘年，至祫之日，別廟後主皆升合食，非無典據。

translations.literal: Thus for more than a hundred years our dynasty has served the ancestral temple, and on the day of the xiá offering the empresses from separate temples all ascend to share the feast—this is not without canonical precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty has maintained the ancestral temple for more than a century, and on xiá days the empresses from separate temples have always joined the communal feast—this is not without canonical authority.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中已曾定議，禮官著酌中之論，先帝有 『恭依』之詔。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong Xiangfu era a decision was already made; the ritual officials set forth a balanced judgment, and the late emperor issued an edict of "respectful compliance."
translations.idiomatic: The matter was already settled in the Dazhong Xiangfu era, when ritual officials issued a balanced ruling and the late emperor approved it with an edict of respectful compliance.

sentences.zh: 他年有司攝事，四後皆預。

translations.literal: In other years when officials performed the rite by proxy, all four empresses participated.
translations.idiomatic: In subsequent years, when officials performed the rites by proxy, all four empresses still participated.

sentences.zh: 今甫欲親祫而四後見黜，不亦疑於以禮之煩故邪？

translations.literal: Now, just as the emperor wishes to perform the xiá in person, the four empresses are to be dismissed—does this not suggest that the trouble of the rite is the real reason?
translations.idiomatic: Now, just as His Majesty wishes to perform the xiá in person, the four empresses are to be excluded—is this not really because the rite has become burdensome?

sentences.zh: 宗廟之禮，至尊至重，苟未能盡祖宗之意，則莫若守舊禮。

translations.literal: The rites of the ancestral temple are supremely exalted and weighty; if one cannot fully fulfill the intentions of the ancestors, then it is best to preserve the old rites.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple rites are the most exalted and solemn of all; if we cannot fully honor our forebears' intentions, we should preserve the established practice.

sentences.zh: 臣等愚以謂 如故便。」

translations.literal: Your subjects in their ignorance consider it best to continue as before."
translations.idiomatic: We humbly recommend that matters continue as before."

sentences.zh: 學士歐陽修等曰：「古者宗廟之制，皆一帝一後。

translations.literal: Academician Ouyang Xiu and others stated: "In antiquity the institution of the ancestral temple assigned one empress to each emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Ouyang Xiu and his colleagues argued: "In antiquity, each emperor in the ancestral temple was paired with a single empress.

sentences.zh: 後世有以子貴者，始著並祔之文，其不當祔者，則有別廟之祭。

translations.literal: In later ages, when a mother was ennobled through her son, provisions for joint enshrinement were first written; those not fit for joint enshrinement received sacrifices at separate temples.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when a mother was honored because her son became emperor, provisions for joint enshrinement were introduced; those not eligible for joint enshrinement received worship at separate temples.

sentences.zh: 本朝禘祫，乃以別廟之後 列於配後之下，非惟於古無文，於今又四不可。

translations.literal: In our dynasty's dì and xiá offerings, empresses from separate temples are ranked below the designated consort—this not only lacks precedent in antiquity but is also impermissible in four ways today.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty's dì and xiá sacrifices, empresses from separate temples are placed below the designated consort—this lacks ancient precedent and is unacceptable in four distinct ways today.

sentences.zh: 淑德，太宗之元配，列於元德之下；

translations.literal: Empress Shude, Taizong's original consort, is ranked below Empress Yuande;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shude, Taizong's original consort, is ranked below Empress Yuande;

sentences.zh: 章懷，真宗之元配，列於章懿之下，一也。

translations.literal: Empress Zhanghuai, Zhenzong's original consort, is ranked below Empress Zhangyi—the first objection.
translations.idiomatic: and Empress Zhanghuai, Zhenzong's original consort, is ranked below Empress Zhangyi—the first objection.

sentences.zh: 升祔之後，統以帝樂；

translations.literal: After joint enshrinement, the imperial hymn is used uniformly;
translations.idiomatic: After joint enshrinement, the imperial hymn is used for all;

sentences.zh: 別廟之後，則 以本室樂章自隨，二也。

translations.literal: empresses from separate temples bring their own shrine hymns— the second objection.
translations.idiomatic: but empresses from separate temples retain their own shrine hymns—the second objection.

sentences.zh: 升祔之後，同牢而祭，牲器祝冊亦統於帝；

translations.literal: After joint enshrinement, they share one pen for the sacrifice, and victims, vessels, and prayer texts are unified under the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: After joint enshrinement, they share one sacrificial pen and victims, vessels, and prayer texts are unified under the emperor;

sentences.zh: 別廟諸後，乃從專享，三也。

translations.literal: empresses of separate temples receive separate offerings—the third objection.
translations.idiomatic: but empresses of separate temples receive separate offerings—the third objection.

sentences.zh: 升祔之後，聯席而坐；

translations.literal: After joint enshrinement, they sit on connected mats;
translations.idiomatic: After joint enshrinement, they sit on connected mats;

sentences.zh: 別廟之後，位乃相絕，四也。

translations.literal: empresses of separate temples sit at a distance from one another—the fourth objection.
translations.idiomatic: but empresses of separate temples are seated far apart—the fourth objection.

sentences.zh: 章獻、章懿在 奉慈廟，每遇禘祫，本廟致享，最為得禮。

translations.literal: Empresses Zhangxian and Zhangyi are in the Fengci Temple; whenever dì or xiá offerings occur, their own temple performs the sacrifice—this is most in accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Empresses Zhangxian and Zhangyi are housed in the Fengci Temple; at each dì and xiá sacrifice, their own temple should perform the offering—this is most proper.

sentences.zh: 若四後各祭於廟，則其尊自申，是於禮無失。

translations.literal: If the four empresses each receive sacrifice at their own temples, their dignity is thereby upheld, and ritual suffers no loss.
translations.idiomatic: If the four empresses each receive sacrifice in their own temples, their dignity is upheld without any breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 以為行之已久，重於改作，則是失禮之舉，無復是正也。

translations.literal: To say that because the practice has long continued, reform is too weighty a matter—this is itself a breach of ritual that can never be set right.
translations.idiomatic: To argue that because the practice has continued so long, reform is too burdensome—is itself a breach of ritual that can never be corrected.

sentences.zh: 請從禮官。」

translations.literal: We request that the ritual officials' view be followed."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the ritual officials' recommendation be adopted."

sentences.zh: 詔：「四後祫享依舊，須大禮畢，別加討論。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "The four empresses shall continue as before at the xiá offering; after the great rite is complete, the matter will be discussed separately."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed: "The four empresses shall continue to participate in the xiá sacrifice as before; after the great ceremony is complete, the matter will be reconsidered separately.

sentences.zh: 仍詔：「祫享前一日，皇帝詣景靈宮，如南郊禮，衛士毋得迎駕呼萬歲。」

translations.literal: A further edict stated: "On the day before the xiá offering, the emperor shall proceed to the Jingling Palace as in the southern suburban rite; the guards must not greet the imperial procession with cries of "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: A further edict directed: "On the day before the xiá sacrifice, the emperor shall visit the Jingling Palace following the southern suburban protocol; guards must not greet the imperial procession with shouts of 'Long live the emperor!'"

sentences.zh: 有司言：「諸司奉禮，攝廩犧令省牲， 依《通禮》改正祀儀。

translations.literal: The responsible officials reported: "The various offices shall perform the ritual offerings; the acting Director of the Imperial Stables and Sacrificial Animals shall inspect the victims, revising the sacrificial protocol according to the Comprehensive Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported: "All departments shall perform their ritual duties; the acting Director of Imperial Stables and Sacrificial Animals shall inspect the victims, revising the sacrificial protocol according to the Comprehensive Rites.

sentences.zh: 散齋四日於別殿，致齋二日於大慶殿，一日於太廟。

translations.literal: Purification without food for four days in a separate hall; full purification for two days in the Hall of Great Celebration, and one day in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shall observe four days of preliminary purification in a separate hall, two days of full purification in the Hall of Great Celebration, and one day in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 尚舍直殿下，設小次，御坐不設黃道褥位。

translations.literal: The Palace Supplies Office shall attend below the palace steps, set up a small resting pavilion, and the imperial seat shall not have the yellow imperial cushion.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Supplies Office shall attend below the palace steps and set up a small resting pavilion; the imperial seat shall not include the yellow imperial cushion.

sentences.zh: 七室各用一太牢，每坐簠簋二，鉶三，籩豆 為後，無黼扆、席幾。

translations.literal: Each of the seven shrines shall use one great offering; at each seat, two grain vessels, three meat vessels, and platters and cups behind—no embroidered screen, mats, or tables.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the seven shrines shall receive one great offering; at each seat there shall be two grain vessels, three meat vessels, and platters and cups arranged behind—without embroidered screens, mats, or tables.

sentences.zh: 出三閣瑞石、篆書玉璽印、青玉環、金山陳於庭。

translations.literal: The auspicious stone from the Three Pavilions, the jade seal with seal-script inscription, the green jade ring, and the golden mountain shall be displayed in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The auspicious stone from the Three Pavilions, the jade seal inscribed in seal script, the green jade ring, and the golden mountain shall be displayed in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 別廟四後合食，牲樂奠拜無異儀。

translations.literal: The four empresses from separate temples shall share the feast; victims, music, offerings, and prostrations shall follow the same protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The four empresses from separate temples shall share the communal feast, with victims, music, offerings, and prostrations following the same protocol.

sentences.zh: 故事，七祀、功臣無牲，止於廟牲肉分割，知廟卿行事。

translations.literal: By precedent, the seven household spirits and meritorious officials received no victims; only portions of the temple victims were divided, and the Director of the Temple conducted the rite.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, the seven household spirits and meritorious officials received no dedicated victims; only portions of the temple victims were divided, and the Director of the Temple conducted the rite.

sentences.zh: 請依《續曲台禮》，共料一羊，而獻官三員，功臣單席，如大中祥符加褥。」

translations.literal: It is requested that according to the Continued Rites of the Qu Terrace, one sheep be shared in common, with three presenting officials, and meritorious officials at separate seats, as in the Dazhong Xiangfu addition of cushions."
translations.idiomatic: It is requested that, following the Continued Rites of the Qu Terrace, one sheep be shared in common, with three presenting officials and meritorious officials at separate seats, as in the Dazhong Xiangfu addition of cushions."

sentences.zh: 十月二日，命樞密副使張望告昊天上帝、皇地祇。

translations.literal: On the second day of the tenth month, Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council Zhang Wang was ordered to announce the rite to the Supreme Lord of Heaven and the Imperial Earth.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the tenth month, Vice Privy Council Commissioner Zhang Wang was ordered to announce the rite to the Supreme Lord of Heaven and the Imperial Earth.

sentences.zh: 帝齋大慶殿。

translations.literal: The emperor purified himself in the Hall of Great Celebration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor observed purification in the Hall of Great Celebration.

sentences.zh: 十一日， 服通天冠、絳紗袍，執圭、乘輿，至大慶殿門外降輿，乘大輦，至天興殿，薦享畢，齋於太廟。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day, wearing the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, holding the scepter and riding the imperial carriage, he alighted outside the Hall of Great Celebration, boarded the great imperial litter, proceeded to the Hall of Heavenly Prosperity to complete the presentation offering, and then observed purification at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh day, wearing the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe, holding the scepter and riding the imperial carriage, he alighted outside the Hall of Great Celebration, boarded the great imperial litter, proceeded to the Hall of Heavenly Prosperity to complete the presentation offering, and then observed purification at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝常服至大次，改袞冕，行禮畢，質明，乘大輦還宮，更服靴 袍，禦紫宸殿，宰臣、百官賀，升宣德門肆赦。

translations.literal: The next day, the emperor in ordinary dress came to the great resting pavilion, changed into the ceremonial robe and crown, completed the rites, and at dawn rode the great litter back to the palace, changed into boots and court robe, presided over the Hall of Purple Brilliance where chief ministers and all officials offered congratulations, and ascended the Xuande Gate to proclaim a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The following day, the emperor arrived at the great resting pavilion in ordinary dress, changed into ceremonial robe and crown, completed the rites, and at dawn rode the great litter back to the palace. He then changed into boots and court robe, presided at the Hall of Purple Brilliance while chief ministers and officials offered congratulations, and ascended the Xuande Gate to proclaim a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，詣諸觀寺行恭謝禮。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day, he proceeded to the various Daoist temples and Buddhist monasteries to perform the thanksgiving rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day, he visited the various Daoist temples and Buddhist monasteries to perform the thanksgiving rite.

sentences.zh: 二十六日，御集英殿為飲福宴。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day, he presided over the Hall for Assembling Excellence for the feast of receiving blessings.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth day, he presided at the Hall for Assembling Excellence for the feast of receiving blessings.

sentences.zh: 治平元年，有司「準畫日，孟冬薦享改為祫祭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiping, the responsible officials reported: "According to the scheduled date, the first-month-of-winter presentation offering is to be changed to a xiá sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiping, the responsible offices reported: "According to the scheduled date, the winter presentation offering is to be changed to a xiá merging sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 按《春秋》，閔公喪未除而行吉

translations.literal: According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, when Duke Min's mourning had not yet ended, an auspicious
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that when Duke Min's mourning had not yet ended, an auspicious

sentences.zh: 禘，《三傳》譏之。

translations.literal: dì sacrifice was performed—the Three Commentaries condemn this.
translations.idiomatic: dì sacrifice was nevertheless performed—and the Three Commentaries condemn it.

sentences.zh: 真宗以咸平二年六月喪除，至十月乃祫祭。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong completed mourning in the sixth month of the second year of Xianping, and only in the tenth month performed the xiá sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong completed mourning in the sixth month of the second year of Xianping but did not perform the xiá sacrifice until the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 天聖元年在諒陰，有司誤通天禧舊禘之數，在再期內按行禘祭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiansheng, while still in mourning seclusion, the officials mistakenly followed the old Tianxi count for dì offerings and performed a dì sacrifice within the second mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiansheng, while the court was still in mourning seclusion, officials mistakenly followed the old Tianxi count for dì sacrifices and performed a dì rite within the second mourning period.

sentences.zh: 以理推之，是二年冬應祫，而誤禘 於元年夏，故四十九年間九禘八祫，例皆太速。

translations.literal: Reasoning from principle, a xiá should have been performed in the winter of the second year, but a dì was mistakenly performed in the summer of the first year; thus over forty-nine years there were nine dì and eight xiá offerings, all too frequent by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: By rights, a xiá should have been held in the winter of the second year, but a dì was mistakenly performed in the summer of the first year; over the next forty-nine years there were nine dì and eight xiá sacrifices, all conducted too frequently.

sentences.zh: 事失於始，則歲月相乘，不得而正。

translations.literal: When the error occurs at the beginning, the months and years multiply upon one another and cannot be set right.
translations.idiomatic: When the error occurs at the outset, the months and years compound upon one another and the schedule can never be corrected.

sentences.zh: 今在大祥內，禮未應袷，明年未禫，亦未應禘，至六月即吉，二月合行祫祭，乞 依舊時享，庶合典禮。」

translations.literal: Now, within the period of great auspicious mourning, a xiá is not ritually due; next year, before the tuo rite, a dì is also not due. Not until the sixth month will the mourning be complete; in the second month a xiá sacrifice would be proper. We beg that the regular seasonal offering be followed instead, so that the canonical rites may be observed."
translations.idiomatic: We are now within the period of great auspicious mourning, when a xiá is not yet due; next year, before the tuo rite, a dì is also not yet due. Mourning will not be complete until the sixth month, and a xiá would be proper only in the second month thereafter. We ask that the regular seasonal offering be performed instead, in accordance with canonical ritual."

sentences.zh: 二年二月，翰林學士王珪等上議曰：「同知太常禮院呂夏卿狀：古者新君踐阼之三年，先君之喪二十七月為禫祭，然後新主祔 廟，特行禘祭，謂之始禘。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others submitted a deliberation: "Associate Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lü Xiaqing reported: In antiquity, in the third year after a new ruler ascended the throne, when the former ruler's twenty-seven-month mourning ended with the tuo rite, the new spirit tablet was enshrined in the temple and a special dì sacrifice was performed, called the inaugural dì.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year, Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others submitted a memorial: "Associate Director Lü Xiaqing of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported that in antiquity, in the third year after a new ruler's accession, when the twenty-seven-month mourning for the late ruler ended with the tuo rite, the new spirit tablet was installed in the temple and a special inaugural dì sacrifice was performed.

sentences.zh: 是冬十月行袷祭，明年又行禘祭，自此五年，再為禘祫。

translations.literal: That winter, in the tenth month, the xiá sacrifice was performed; the following year the dì sacrifice was performed again; from then on, every five years, dì and xiá were performed alternately.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, the xiá sacrifice was performed; the following year the dì sacrifice was performed; thereafter, every five years, dì and xiá alternated.

sentences.zh: 喪除必有禘祫者，為再大祭之本也。

translations.literal: That mourning must end with dì and xiá offerings is because they form the foundation of the two great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The dì and xiá sacrifices at the end of mourning are foundational to the two great periodic sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 今當袷祭，緣陛下未終三年之制，納有司之 說，十月依舊時享。

translations.literal: Now a xiá sacrifice is due, but because Your Majesty has not yet completed the three-year mourning period, accepting the officials' proposal, the tenth month will follow the regular seasonal offering.
translations.idiomatic: A xiá sacrifice is now due, but because Your Majesty has not yet completed the three-year mourning period, accepting the officials' proposal, the tenth month will follow the regular seasonal offering instead.

sentences.zh: 然享廟、袷祭，其禮不同。

translations.literal: Yet the temple offering and the xiá sacrifice follow different rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the regular temple offering and the xiá sacrifice follow different protocols.

sentences.zh: 故事，郊享之年遇祫未嘗權罷，唯罷臘祭。

translations.literal: By precedent, in years when suburban sacrifices were performed, if a xiá fell due it was never provisionally suspended—only the la offering was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, in years when suburban sacrifices were performed, a due xiá was never provisionally canceled—only the year-end la offering was suspended.

sentences.zh: 是則孟享與享廟嘗並行於季冬矣。

translations.literal: Thus the first-month offering and the temple offering have sometimes been performed together in the last month of winter.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the first-month offering and the regular temple offering have sometimes been performed together in the last month of winter.

sentences.zh: 其禘祫年數，乞一依太常禮院請，今年 十月行祫祭，明年四月行禘祭。

translations.literal: As for the interval for dì and xiá offerings, we beg that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' request be followed entirely: perform the xiá sacrifice this year in the tenth month, and the dì sacrifice next year in the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: As for the interval between dì and xiá sacrifices, we ask that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' recommendation be followed: perform the xiá sacrifice this year in the tenth month and the dì sacrifice next year in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 仍如夏卿議。」

translations.literal: This shall still follow Xiaqing's deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: This shall follow Director Xiaqing's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 權罷今年臘享。

translations.literal: The la offering for this year was provisionally suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The year-end la offering for this year was provisionally suspended.

sentences.zh: 熙寧八年，有司言：「已尊僖祖為太廟始祖，孟夏禘祭，當正東向之位。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xining, the responsible officials reported: "Emperor Xi has already been honored as the founding ancestor of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; at the first-month-of-summer dì sacrifice, he should be given the correct east-facing position."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xining, the responsible offices reported: "Now that Emperor Xi has been honored as the founding ancestor of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, at the summer dì sacrifice he should occupy the correct east-facing seat.

sentences.zh: 又言：「太廟禘祭神位，已尊始祖居東向之位，自順祖而下，昭、穆各以南北為序。

translations.literal: They further reported: "For the spirit tablets at the dì sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the founding ancestor has already been given the east-facing position; from Emperor Shun downward, the zhao and mu lines are each ordered north and south.
translations.idiomatic: They further reported: "At the dì sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the founding ancestor now occupies the east-facing seat; from Emperor Shun downward, the zhao and mu lines are ordered north and south respectively.

sentences.zh: 自今禘祫，著為定禮。」

translations.literal: From now on, for dì and xiá offerings, this shall be established as the fixed rite."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, for all dì and xiá sacrifices, this shall be established as the fixed protocol."

sentences.zh: 元豐四年，詳定郊廟禮文所言：「禘祫之義，存於《周禮》、《春秋》，而不著其名。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, the office for determining suburban and temple ritual texts stated: "The meaning of the dì and xiá offerings is preserved in the Rites of Zhou and the Spring and Autumn Annals, but the names are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, the office for determining suburban and temple ritual texts stated: "The meaning of the dì and xiá sacrifices is preserved in the Rites of Zhou and the Spring and Autumn Annals, though the terms themselves are not recorded there.

sentences.zh: 行禮之年，經皆無文，唯《公羊傳》曰：『五年而再盛祭。』

translations.literal: The years when these rites were performed are nowhere specified in the classics; only the Gongyang Commentary states: 'Every five years there is another great sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: The years when these rites were to be performed are nowhere specified in the classics; only the Gongyang Commentary states, 'Every five years there is another great sacrifice.'

sentences.zh: 《禮緯》 曰：『三年一祫，五年一禘。』

translations.literal: The Apocrypha on the Rites states: 'Once every three years a xiá; once every five years a dì.'
translations.idiomatic: The Apocrypha on the Rites states, 'A xiá every three years, a dì every five years.'

sentences.zh: 而又分為二說：鄭氏則曰：『前三後二』，謂禘後四十二月而祫，祫後十八月而禘。

translations.literal: These further divide into two schools: Master Zheng says 'three before, two after,' meaning that twelve months after a dì comes a xiá, and eighteen months after a xiá comes a dì.
translations.idiomatic: Two schools of interpretation emerged: Master Zheng's 'three before, two after' holds that a xiá follows a dì by twelve months, and a dì follows a xiá by eighteen months.

sentences.zh: 徐邈則曰：『前二後三』，謂二祭相去各三十 月。

translations.literal: Xu Miao says 'two before, three after,' meaning that the two sacrifices are each thirty months apart.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao's 'two before, three after' holds that the two sacrifices are each thirty months apart.

sentences.zh: 以二說考之，惟鄭氏曰：『魯禮，三年喪畢，祫於太廟，明年禘於群廟，自後五年而再盛祭，一祫一禘。』

translations.literal: Comparing the two schools, only Master Zheng states: 'In the rites of Lu, when the three-year mourning was complete, a xiá was performed at the Grand Temple; the following year a dì at the group of temples; thereafter every five years the two great sacrifices alternated, one xiá and one dì.'
translations.idiomatic: Comparing the two schools, only Master Zheng's account is well supported: 'In the rites of Lu, when the three-year mourning ended, a xiá was performed at the Grand Temple; the following year a dì at the group of temples; thereafter every five years the two great sacrifices alternated, one xiá and one dì.

sentences.zh: 實為有據。

translations.literal: This truly has canonical support.
translations.idiomatic: This account has solid canonical support.

sentences.zh: 本朝慶曆初用徐邈說，每三十月一祭。

translations.literal: Our dynasty at the beginning of Qingli adopted Xu Miao's view, performing a sacrifice every thirty months.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty initially adopted Xu Miao's view at the beginning of the Qingli era, performing a sacrifice every thirty months.

sentences.zh: 熙 寧八年，既禘而祫，此有司之失也。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xining, a dì was performed and then a xiá—this was the officials' error.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xining, a dì was followed immediately by a xiá—this was the officials' error.

sentences.zh: 請今十八月而禘，禘四十二月而祫，庶幾舉禮不煩，事神不瀆。」

translations.literal: We request that now a dì be performed after eighteen months, and a xiá twelve months after a dì, so that performing the rites is not burdensome and serving the spirits is not irreverent."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that a dì now be performed eighteen months after a xiá, and a xiá twelve months after a dì, so that the rites are not performed too frequently and the spirits are not treated irreverently.

sentences.zh: 太常禮院言：「本朝自慶曆以來，皆三十月而一祭。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices stated: "Since the Qingli era, our dynasty has performed a sacrifice every thirty months.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices replied: "Since the Qingli era, our dynasty has performed a sacrifice every thirty months.

sentences.zh: 至熙寧五 年後，始不通計，遂至八年禘祫並在一歲。

translations.literal: After the fifth year of Xining, the count was no longer kept properly, so that by the eighth year both dì and xiá were performed in a single year.
translations.idiomatic: After the fifth year of Xining, the schedule was no longer properly tracked, so that by the eighth year both dì and xiá were performed in a single year.

sentences.zh: 昨元豐三年四月已行禘禮，今年若依舊例，十月行祫享，即比年頻袷，復踵前失。

translations.literal: Last year, in the fourth month of the third year of Yuanfeng, the dì rite was already performed; if this year the old precedent is followed and a xiá offering is performed in the tenth month, then xiá offerings will again be too frequent, repeating the earlier error.
translations.idiomatic: The dì rite was already performed in the fourth month of the third year of Yuanfeng; if the old precedent is followed and a xiá sacrifice is held this October, xiá sacrifices will again be too frequent, repeating the earlier error.

sentences.zh: 請依慶曆以來之制，通計年數，皆三十 月而祭。」

translations.literal: We request that the institution since Qingli be followed, counting the years comprehensively, with a sacrifice every thirty months."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the practice in force since the Qingli era be followed, counting the years comprehensively so that a sacrifice is held every thirty months.

sentences.zh: 詔如見行典禮。

translations.literal: An edict directed that the currently practiced canonical rites be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed that the rites currently in practice be followed.

sentences.zh: 詳定所又言：「古者稞獻、饋食，禴祠、烝、嘗，並為先王之享，未嘗廢一時之祭。

translations.literal: The office for determining ritual texts further stated: "In antiquity, the libation presentation, the feeding offering, the yue sacrifice, the zheng and chang offerings were all sacrifices of the former kings, and not one seasonal sacrifice was ever abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The office for determining ritual texts further stated: "In antiquity, the libation presentation, feeding offering, yue sacrifice, and zheng and chang seasonal offerings were all sacrifices of the former kings, and no seasonal sacrifice was ever abandoned.

sentences.zh: 故孔氏《正義》以為：『天子夏為大祭 之禘，不廢時祭之礿；

translations.literal: Therefore the Correct Meaning of the Kong clan holds: 'When the Son of Heaven in summer performs the great dì sacrifice, he does not abolish the seasonal yue offering;
translations.idiomatic: The Correct Meaning of the Kong commentary therefore holds: 'When the Son of Heaven in summer performs the great dì sacrifice, he does not abolish the seasonal yue offering;

sentences.zh: 秋為大祭之祫，不廢時祭之嘗。』

translations.literal: in autumn he performs the great xiá sacrifice, and does not abolish the seasonal chang offering.'
translations.idiomatic: in autumn he performs the great xiá sacrifice, and does not abolish the seasonal chang offering.

sentences.zh: 則王禮三年一袷與禘享，更為時祭。

translations.literal: Thus in royal rites, the xiá and dì every three years alternate with the seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in royal rites, the three-year xiá and five-year dì alternate with the seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 本朝沿襲故常，久未厘正，請每禘祫之月雖已大祭，仍行時享，以嚴天 子備禮，所以丕崇祖宗之義。

translations.literal: Our dynasty has inherited this constant practice and long failed to rectify it. We request that even in months when dì or xiá sacrifices are performed, the seasonal offering still be conducted, so that the Son of Heaven's full ritual observance may be strict—this is how the exaltation of the ancestors is to be upheld.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty has long inherited this practice without correcting it. We ask that even in months when dì or xiá sacrifices are performed, the seasonal offering still be conducted, so that the Son of Heaven fully observes his rites and thereby exalts the ancestors as intended.

sentences.zh: 其郊禮、親祠準此。」

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifices and personal temple sacrifices should follow this rule."
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifices and sacrifices at which the emperor attends in person should follow this rule."

sentences.zh: 又言：「《禮》：不王不禘。

translations.literal: They further stated: "The Rites say: Without being king, one does not perform the dì.
translations.idiomatic: They further stated: "The Rites say: Without being king, one does not perform the dì.

sentences.zh: 虞、夏、商、周四代所禘，皆以帝有天下，其世係所出者明，故追祭 所及者遠也。

translations.literal: In the Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties, those honored in the dì all possessed the realm under Heaven; their lineages of descent were clear, and therefore the ancestors reached back in sacrifice were remote.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties, those honored in the dì all ruled the realm; their lines of descent were clear, and therefore the ancestors reached in sacrifice lay far back in time.

sentences.zh: 太祖受命，祭四親廟，推僖祖而上所自出者，譜失其傳，有司因仍舊說，禘祫皆合群廟之主，綴食於始祖，失禮莫甚。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the Mandate, he sacrificed at the temples of four close forebears; tracing upward from Emperor Xi to the one from whom the line sprang, the genealogy was lost. The officials perpetuated the old account, and at dì and xiá all grouped the lords of the collective temples and attached them to the founding ancestor—nothing was more contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu received the Mandate, he sacrificed at the temples of four close forebears; but tracing upward from Emperor Xi to the dynastic founder, the genealogy was lost. Officials perpetuated the old account, and at dì and xiá grouped all temple lords together and attached them to the founding ancestor—nothing was more contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 今國家世係與四代不同，既求其 祖之所自出而不得，則禘禮當闕，必推見祖係乃可以行。」

translations.literal: Now our dynasty's lineage differs from the four dynasties. Since the ancestor from whom the line sprang cannot be found, the dì rite ought to be omitted; only when the ancestral line can be traced may it be performed."
translations.idiomatic: Now our dynasty's lineage differs from those four dynasties. Since the dynastic founder cannot be identified, the dì rite ought to be omitted; only when the ancestral line can be established may it be performed."

sentences.zh: 神宗謂輔臣曰：「禘者，本以審禘祖之所自出，故禮，不王不禘。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said to his chief ministers: "The dì is fundamentally for examining and sorting the ancestor from whom the line sprang; therefore the rites say, without being king, one does not perform the dì.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong told his chief ministers: "The dì exists fundamentally to identify the ancestor from whom the line sprang; hence the rites say that without being king one does not perform the dì.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢以後，譜牒不明，莫知其祖之所 自出，由禘禮可廢也。」

translations.literal: After the Qin and Han, genealogies were unclear and no one knew from whom the ancestor sprang; therefore the dì rite could be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: After the Qin and Han, genealogies were unclear and no one knew the dynastic founder; therefore the dì rite could be abolished."

sentences.zh: 已而詳定所言：「古者天子祭宗廟，有堂事焉，有室事焉。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the determining office stated: "In antiquity when the Son of Heaven sacrificed at the ancestral temple, there were hall rites and chamber rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the determining office stated: "In antiquity when the Son of Heaven sacrificed at the ancestral temple, there were hall rites and chamber rites.

sentences.zh: 按《禮》，祝延屍入奧，灌後乃出延牲，延屍主出於室，坐於堂 上，始祖南面，昭在東，穆在西，乃行朝踐之禮，是堂事也。

translations.literal: According to the Rites, after the invocator extended the corpse into the inner recess and libation was poured, the victim was brought out and the spirit tablet was extended; the spirit tablet was brought out from the chamber and seated in the hall, with the founding ancestor facing south, the zhao in the east and the mu in the west—then the morning presentation rite was performed; this was the hall rite.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Rites, after the invocator extended the corpse into the inner recess and libation was poured, the victim was brought out and the spirit tablet extended; the tablet was brought from the chamber and seated in the hall, with the founding ancestor facing south and the zhao in the east and mu in the west—then the morning presentation was performed; this was the hall rite.

sentences.zh: 設饌於堂，復延主入室，始祖東面，昭南穆北，徙常上之饌於室中，乃行饋食之禮，是室事也。

translations.literal: Food was set in the hall, then the tablet was again extended into the chamber; the founding ancestor faced east, the zhao south and the mu north, and the food normally on the upper mat was moved into the chamber—then the feeding rite was performed; this was the chamber rite.
translations.idiomatic: Food was set in the hall, then the tablet was brought back into the chamber; the founding ancestor faced east, the zhao south and the mu north, and the food from the upper mat was moved into the chamber—then the feeding rite was performed; this was the chamber rite.

sentences.zh: 請每行 大祫，堂上設南面之位，室中設東面之位。」

translations.literal: We request that whenever the great xiá is performed, a south-facing seat be set in the hall and an east-facing seat in the chamber."
translations.idiomatic: We request that at each great xiá sacrifice, a south-facing seat be set in the hall and an east-facing seat in the chamber.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「合食之禮，始祖東面、昭南穆北者，本室中之位也。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites stated: "In the rite of shared feasting, the founding ancestor faces east and the zhao south and mu north—these are positions within the chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites replied: "In the rite of shared feasting, the founding ancestor faces east with the zhao south and mu north—these are chamber positions.

sentences.zh: 今設位戶外，祖宗昭、穆別為幄次，殆非合食之義。

translations.literal: Now seats are set outside the doors, and the ancestors of the zhao and mu are separated into distinct enclosures—this is hardly in keeping with the meaning of shared feasting.
translations.idiomatic: Now seats are set outside the doors with zhao and mu ancestors in separate enclosures—this hardly accords with shared feasting.

sentences.zh: 請 自今祫享，即前楹通設帳幕，以應室中之位。」

translations.literal: We request that from this xiá offering onward, canopy tents be set across the front pillars to correspond to the chamber positions."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that from this xiá offering onward, canopy tents be set across the front pillars to correspond to the chamber positions."

sentences.zh: 大觀四年，議禮局請：「每大祫，堂上設南面之位，室中設東南之位，始祖南面則昭穆東西相向，始祖東面則昭穆南北相向，以應古義。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daguan, the Bureau for Deliberating Rites requested: "At each great xiá, a south-facing seat shall be set in the hall and a southeast-facing seat in the chamber; when the founding ancestor faces south, the zhao and mu face each other east and west; when the founding ancestor faces east, the zhao and mu face each other north and south—to accord with ancient meaning."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daguan, the Bureau for Deliberating Rites requested: "At each great xiá, a south-facing seat shall be set in the hall and a southeast-facing seat in the chamber; when the founding ancestor faces south, zhao and mu face east and west; when he faces east, zhao and mu face north and south—in accord with ancient usage.

sentences.zh: 又請：「陳瑞物及代國之寶與貢物可出而陳者，並令有司依嘉祐、元豐詔旨，凡親祠太廟準此。」

translations.literal: They further requested: "Auspicious objects and treasures of successive dynasties, together with tribute items that may be displayed, shall all be arranged by the responsible offices according to the edicts of the Jiayou and Yuanfeng eras; all personal sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple shall follow this."
translations.idiomatic: They further requested that auspicious objects and treasures of successive dynasties, together with displayable tribute items, be arranged by the responsible offices according to the Jiayou and Yuanfeng edicts, and that all sacrifices at which the emperor attends in person at the Imperial Ancestral Temple follow this rule."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 南渡之後，有祫而無禘。

translations.literal: After the southward relocation, there were xiá offerings but no dì.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward relocation, xiá sacrifices were performed but not dì sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎二年，祫享於洪州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan under Emperor Gaozong, a xiá offering was performed at Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan, Emperor Gaozong performed a xiá sacrifice at Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，祫享於溫州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, a xiá offering was performed at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing, a xiá sacrifice was performed at Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 時儀文草創，奉遷祖宗及祧廟神主、別廟神主，各設幄合食於太廟。

translations.literal: At that time the ritual texts were newly devised; the spirit tablets of the relocated ancestors, the removed-branch temple tablets, and the separate-temple tablets were each placed in enclosures and shared the feast at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At that time ritual protocols were newly devised; spirit tablets of the relocated ancestors, removed-branch temples, and separate temples were each placed in enclosures to share the feast at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 始祖東向，昭、穆以次南北相向。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor faced east, and the zhao and mu were arranged north and south in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor faced east, with zhao and mu arranged alternately north and south.

sentences.zh: 五年，吏部員外郎董弅言：「臣聞戎、祀，國之大事，而宗廟之祭，又祀之大者也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel Dong Bian stated: "I have heard that military affairs and sacrifices are great affairs of state, and sacrifice at the ancestral temple is the greatest among sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Dong Bian, supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, stated: "I have heard that military affairs and sacrifices are great affairs of state, and ancestral temple sacrifice is the greatest among sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大祀，禘祫為重，祫大禘小，則袷為莫大焉。

translations.literal: Among great sacrifices, dì and xiá are paramount; xiá is greater than dì, so the xiá is the greatest of all.
translations.idiomatic: Among great sacrifices, dì and xiá are paramount; xiá is greater than dì, so the xiá is supreme.

sentences.zh: 今戎事方殷，祭祀之禮未暇遍 舉，然事有違經戾古，上不當天地神祇之意，下未合億兆黎庶之心，特出於一時大臣好勝之臆說，而行之六十年未有知其非者。

translations.literal: Now military affairs are pressing and the full round of sacrifices cannot be performed everywhere; yet there are matters that violate the classics and depart from antiquity, failing to satisfy Heaven, Earth, and the spirits above or the hearts of the myriad people below—arising solely from the presumptuous theories of chief ministers eager to prevail, practiced for sixty years without anyone recognizing their error.
translations.idiomatic: Now military affairs are pressing and sacrifices cannot all be performed; yet some practices violate the classics and antiquity, failing to satisfy Heaven, Earth, and the spirits above or the people below—arising solely from presumptuous theories of rival ministers, practiced for sixty years without recognition of error.

sentences.zh: 顧雖治兵禦戎之際，正厥違誤，宜不 可緩。

translations.literal: Even amid organizing armies and repelling invaders, to correct these errors ought not be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Even while organizing armies and repelling invaders, correcting these errors ought not be delayed.

sentences.zh: 仰惟太祖受天明命，混一區宇，即其功德所起，宜祇享以正東向之尊。

translations.literal: Reflect that Taizu received the Mandate of Heaven and unified the realm; considering where his merit began, he ought to be honored with the due dignity of the east-facing seat.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu received the Mandate of Heaven and unified the realm; considering where his merit began, he ought to receive the due dignity of the east-facing seat.

sentences.zh: 逮至仁宗，親行祫享，嘗議太祖東向，用昭正統之緒。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Renzong, who personally performed the xiá sacrifice, it was once debated that Taizu should face east, thereby clarifying the legitimate succession.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Renzong's time, when he personally performed the xiá sacrifice, it was debated that Taizu should face east to clarify the legitimate succession.

sentences.zh: 當時在廷之臣，僉謂自古必以受 命之祖乃居東向之位，本朝太祖乃受命之君，若論七廟之次，有僖祖以降四廟在上，當時大祫，止列昭穆而虛東向，蓋終不敢以非受命之祖而居之也。

translations.literal: The ministers at court then unanimously said that since antiquity the ancestor who received the Mandate must occupy the east-facing seat; in our dynasty Taizu was the ruler who received the Mandate. If one considers the order of the seven temples, four temples from Emperor Xi upward stood above him; at the great xiá of that time, only the zhao and mu were arrayed while the east-facing seat was left vacant—because in the end they did not dare place one who had not received the Mandate in that seat.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers then unanimously held that since antiquity only the ancestor who received the Mandate occupies the east-facing seat, and Taizu was our dynasty's recipient of the Mandate; yet with four temples above him from Emperor Xi onward, at the great xiá only zhao and mu were arrayed while the east-facing seat was left vacant—because they dared not seat one who had not received the Mandate there.

sentences.zh: 暨熙寧之初， 僖祖以世次當祧，禮官韓維等據經有請，適王安石用事，奮其臆說，乃俾章衡建議，尊僖祖為始祖，肇居東向。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Xining, when Emperor Xi by generational order was due for removal, ritual officials such as Han Wei petitioned on canonical grounds; just then Wang Anshi was in power and pressed his private theory, causing Zhang Heng to propose honoring Emperor Xi as founding ancestor and placing him first in the east-facing seat.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of Xining, when Emperor Xi was due for removal by generational order, ritual officials including Han Wei petitioned on canonical grounds; Wang Anshi was then in power and pressed his private theory, causing Zhang Heng to propose honoring Emperor Xi as founding ancestor in the east-facing seat.

sentences.zh: 馮京奏謂士大夫以太祖不得東向為恨，安石肆言以折 之。

translations.literal: Feng Jing memorialized that scholar-officials resented that Taizu could not face east; Anshi spoke boldly to refute them.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jing memorialized that scholar-officials resented Taizu's inability to face east; Anshi spoke boldly to refute them.

sentences.zh: 已而又欲罷太祖郊配，神宗以太祖開基受命，不許，安石終不以為然。

translations.literal: Later he also wished to abolish Taizu's pairing at the suburban sacrifice; Emperor Shenzong, holding that Taizu founded the dynasty and received the Mandate, did not permit it, yet Anshi never accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also wished to abolish Taizu's pairing at the suburban sacrifice; Shenzong, holding that Taizu founded the dynasty and received the Mandate, refused, yet Anshi never accepted this.

sentences.zh: 元祐之初，翼祖既祧，正合典禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, when Emperor Yi was removed, this accorded with canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanyou, when Emperor Yi was removed, this accorded with canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 至於崇寧，宣祖當祧，適蔡京用事，一遵安石之術，乃 建言請立九廟，自我作古，其已祧翼祖、宣祖並即依舊。

translations.literal: By Chongning, when Emperor Xuan was due for removal, Cai Jing was in power and followed Anshi's method entirely; he proposed establishing nine temples, creating antiquity anew, and restored the removed Emperors Yi and Xuan as before.
translations.idiomatic: By Chongning, when Emperor Xuan was due for removal, Cai Jing followed Anshi's method entirely, proposing nine temples and creating antiquity anew, while restoring the removed Emperors Yi and Xuan.

sentences.zh: 循沿至今，太祖尚居第四室，遇大祫處昭穆之列。

translations.literal: Down to the present, Taizu still occupies the fourth shrine; at the great xiá he is placed among the zhao and mu.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the present Taizu still occupies the fourth shrine and at the great xiá is placed among the zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 今若正太祖東向之尊，委合《禮經》。」

translations.literal: If Taizu's east-facing dignity is now rectified, it will accord with the Ritual Canon."
translations.idiomatic: If Taizu's east-facing dignity is now rectified, it will accord with the Ritual Canon."

sentences.zh: 太 常寺丞王普又言：「弅所奏深得禮意，而其言尚有未盡。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Pu further stated: "Bian's memorial deeply accords with ritual intent, yet his words do not go far enough.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director Wang Pu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices further stated: "Bian's memorial deeply accords with ritual intent, yet does not go far enough.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以古者廟製異宮，則太祖居中，而群廟列其左右；

translations.literal: Your subject considers that in antiquity when temples were separate structures, Taizu stood in the center and the group of temples were arrayed to his left and right;
translations.idiomatic: I consider that in antiquity, when temples were separate structures, Taizu stood at the center with the group of temples to his left and right;

sentences.zh: 後世廟製同堂，則太祖居右，而諸室皆列其左。

translations.literal: in later ages when temples shared one hall, Taizu stood on the right and all shrines were arrayed to his left.
translations.idiomatic: in later ages, when temples shared one hall, Taizu stood on the right with all shrines to his left.

sentences.zh: 古者 祫享，朝踐於堂，則太祖南向，而昭穆位於東西；

translations.literal: In antiquity at the xiá offering, the morning presentation was in the hall, with Taizu facing south and the zhao and mu placed east and west;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity at the xiá, the morning presentation was in the hall, with Taizu facing south and zhao and mu east and west;

sentences.zh: 饋食於室，則太祖東向，而昭穆位於南北。

translations.literal: the feeding rite was in the chamber, with Taizu facing east and the zhao and mu placed north and south.
translations.idiomatic: the feeding rite was in the chamber, with Taizu facing east and zhao and mu north and south.

sentences.zh: 後世祫享一於堂上，而用室中之位，故唯以東向為太祖之尊焉。

translations.literal: In later ages the xiá was performed entirely in the hall using chamber positions; therefore only the east-facing seat expressed Taizu's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages the xiá was performed entirely in the hall using chamber positions; only the east-facing seat expressed Taizu's dignity.

sentences.zh: 若夫群 廟迭毀，而太祖不遷，則其禮尚矣。

translations.literal: As for the successive removal of the group of temples while Taizu was not moved, that rite was still honored.
translations.idiomatic: As for the successive removal of other temples while Taizu was not moved, that rite was still honored.

sentences.zh: 臣故知太祖即廟之始祖，是為廟號，非諡號也。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore knows that Taizu is the founding ancestor of the temple—this is a temple title, not a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore know that Taizu is the temple's founding ancestor—this is a temple title, not a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 惟我太宗嗣服之初，太祖廟號已定，雖更累朝，世次猶近，每於祫享，必虛東向 之位，以其非太祖必不可居也。

translations.literal: When our Taizong first succeeded to the throne, Taizu's temple title was already fixed; though many reigns passed and the generations were still near, at each xiá the east-facing seat was always left vacant, because he was not Taizu and certainly could not occupy it.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong first succeeded, Taizu's temple title was already fixed; though generations passed, at each xiá the east-facing seat was left vacant, because only Taizu could occupy it.

sentences.zh: 迨至熙寧，又尊僖祖為廟之始祖，百世不遷，祫享東向，而太祖常居穆位，則名實舛矣。

translations.literal: By Xining, Emperor Xi was again honored as the temple's founding ancestor, never to be removed, and at the xiá faced east while Taizu constantly occupied the mu position—then name and reality were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: By Xining, Emperor Xi was again honored as founding ancestor, never removed, facing east at the xiá while Taizu occupied the mu position—then name and reality diverged.

sentences.zh: 倘以熙寧之禮為是，僖祖當稱太祖，而太祖 當改廟號。

translations.literal: If the Xining rite were correct, Emperor Xi should be called Taizu and Taizu's temple title should be changed.
translations.idiomatic: If the Xining rite were correct, Emperor Xi should be called Taizu and Taizu's temple title changed.

sentences.zh: 然則太祖之名不正，前日之失大矣。

translations.literal: Then Taizu's name would not be correct, and the error of former days would be great.
translations.idiomatic: Then Taizu's name would be incorrect and the former error would be grave.

sentences.zh: 今宜奉太祖神主居第一室，永為廟之始祖。

translations.literal: Now Taizu's spirit tablet should be placed in the first shrine, permanently the temple's founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's spirit tablet should now be placed in the first shrine as the temple's permanent founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 每歲五享、告朔、薦新，止於七廟。

translations.literal: The five annual offerings, new-moon and full-moon reports, and new-harvest presentations should be limited to the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: The five annual offerings, new- and full-moon reports, and new-harvest presentations should be limited to the seven temples.

sentences.zh: 三年一祫，則太祖正東向之位。

translations.literal: Once every three years at the xiá, Taizu should occupy the correct east-facing seat.
translations.idiomatic: Once every three years at the xiá, Taizu should occupy the correct east-facing seat.

sentences.zh: 太 宗、仁宗、神宗南向為昭，真宗、英宗、哲宗北向為穆。

translations.literal: Taizong, Renzong, and Shenzong should face south as zhao; Zhenzong, Yingzong, and Zhezong should face north as mu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, Renzong, and Shenzong should face south as zhao; Zhenzong, Yingzong, and Zhezong north as mu.

sentences.zh: 五年一禘，則迎宣祖神主享於太廟，而以太祖配焉。

translations.literal: Once every five years at the dì, Emperor Xuan's spirit tablet should be brought to the Imperial Ancestral Temple with Taizu as his paired ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Once every five years at the dì, Emperor Xuan's tablet should be brought to the Imperial Ancestral Temple with Taizu as paired ancestor.

sentences.zh: 如是，則宗廟之事盡合《禮經》，無復前日之失矣。」

translations.literal: In this way, ancestral temple affairs would fully accord with the Ritual Canon and the errors of former days would be undone."
translations.idiomatic: Thus ancestral temple affairs would fully accord with the Ritual Canon and former errors undone.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「太祖皇帝開基創業，始受天命，祫享宜居東向之位。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Emperor Taizu founded the dynasty and first received the Mandate; at the xiá he ought to occupy the east-facing seat."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Emperor Taizu founded the dynasty and first received the Mandate; at the xiá he ought to occupy the east-facing seat."

sentences.zh: 宰相趙鼎等奏曰：「三昭三穆，與太祖之廟而七，載在《禮經》，無可疑者。」

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Zhao Ding and others memorialized: "Three zhao and three mu, together with Taizu's temple making seven, are recorded in the Ritual Canon—there is no doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Zhao Ding and others memorialized: "Three zhao and three mu together with Taizu's temple make seven, as recorded in the Ritual Canon—there is no doubt."

sentences.zh: 紹熙五 年九月，太常少卿曾三復亦言：請祧宣祖，就正太祖東向之位，其言甚切。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Shaoxi, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zeng Sanfu also petitioned to remove Emperor Xuan and rectify Taizu's east-facing seat; his words were very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Shaoxi, Vice Director Zeng Sanfu also petitioned to remove Emperor Xuan and rectify Taizu's east-facing seat in earnest terms.

sentences.zh: 既而吏部尚書鄭僑等亦乞因大行祔廟之際，定宗廟萬世之禮，慰太祖在天之靈，破熙寧不 經之論。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, Minister of Personnel Zheng Qiao and others also begged that at the installation of the new spirit tablet during the great mourning, the ancestral temple rite for ten thousand generations be settled to comfort Taizu in Heaven and refute the uncanonical theory of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Minister Zheng Qiao and others begged that at installation of the new spirit tablet during great mourning, the eternal ancestral temple rite be settled to comfort Taizu in Heaven and refute Xining's uncanonical theory.

sentences.zh: 今太祖為始祖，則太宗為昭，真宗為穆，自是而下以至孝宗，四昭四穆與太祖之廟而九。

translations.literal: Now with Taizu as founding ancestor, Taizong is zhao, Zhenzong is mu, and from there down to Xiaozong—four zhao and four mu together with Taizu's temple make nine.
translations.idiomatic: With Taizu as founding ancestor, Taizong is zhao, Zhenzong mu, and down to Xiaozong—four zhao and four mu with Taizu's temple make nine.

sentences.zh: 上參古禮，而不廢崇寧九廟之制，於義為允。

translations.literal: The emperor consulted ancient ritual yet did not abolish the nine-temple system of Chongning—in principle this was acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted ancient ritual yet did not abolish Chongning's nine-temple system—in principle this was acceptable.

sentences.zh: 又言：「治平四年， 僖祖祧遷，藏在西夾室。

translations.literal: They further stated: "In the fourth year of Zhiping, Emperor Xi was removed and his tablet stored in the western side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: They further stated: "In the fourth year of Zhiping, Emperor Xi was removed and stored in the western side chamber.

sentences.zh: 至熙寧五年，王安石以私意使章衡等議，乃復祔僖祖以為始祖，又將推以配天，欲罷太祖郊配。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining, Wang Anshi by private intent had Zhang Heng and others deliberate and restored Emperor Xi as founding ancestor; he also wished to promote him to pair with Heaven and abolish Taizu's pairing at the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xining, Wang Anshi had Zhang Heng and others restore Emperor Xi as founding ancestor by private intent and wished to promote him to pair with Heaven and abolish Taizu's suburban pairing.

sentences.zh: 韓維、司馬光等力爭，而安石主其說愈堅。

translations.literal: Han Wei, Sima Guang, and others strove against this, while Anshi held to his view ever more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wei, Sima Guang, and others strove against this while Anshi held ever more firmly to his view.

sentences.zh: 孫固慮其罷太祖配天，建議以僖祖權居東向之位。

translations.literal: Sun Gu, fearing abolition of Taizu's heavenly pairing, proposed that Emperor Xi provisionally occupy the east-facing seat.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gu, fearing abolition of Taizu's heavenly pairing, proposed that Emperor Xi provisionally occupy the east-facing seat.

sentences.zh: 既曰權居，則當厘正明矣。」

translations.literal: Since it was called provisional, rectification should have been clear."
translations.idiomatic: Since it was called provisional, rectification should have been clear.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 閏十月，權禮部侍郎許及之言：「僖、順、翼、宣四祖，為太 祖之祖考，所遷之主，恐不得藏於子孫之廟。

translations.literal: In the intercalary tenth month, Acting Vice Minister of Rites Xu Jizhi stated: "Emperors Xi, Shun, Yi, and Xuan, as Taizu's forebears—the removed tablets probably ought not be stored in descendants' temples.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary tenth month, Acting Vice Minister Xu Jizhi stated: "Emperors Xi, Shun, Yi, and Xuan, as Taizu's forebears—their removed tablets probably ought not be stored in descendants' temples.

sentences.zh: 今順、翼二祖藏於西夾室，實居太廟太祖之右。

translations.literal: Now the tablets of Emperors Shun and Yi are stored in the western side chamber, actually to the right of Taizu in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Shun and Yi are now stored in the western side chamber, actually to Taizu's right in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 遇祫享，則於夾室之前，設位以昭穆焉。」

translations.literal: When a xiá is performed, seats are set before the side chamber according to zhao and mu."
translations.idiomatic: At the xiá, seats are set before the side chamber according to zhao and mu.

sentences.zh: 於是詔有司集議，吏部尚書 兼侍讀鄭僑等言：「僖祖當用唐興聖之制，立為別廟，順祖、翼祖、宣祖之主皆祔藏焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered officials to assemble for deliberation. Zheng Qiao, Minister of Personnel and Imperial Reader, and others stated: "Emperor Xi should follow the Tang system for Emperor Xingsheng, established as a separate temple, with the tablets of Emperors Shun, Yi, and Xuan enshrined there.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered deliberation. Zheng Qiao, Minister of Personnel and Imperial Reader, and others stated: "Emperor Xi should follow the Tang system for Emperor Xingsheng as a separate temple, with Emperors Shun, Yi, and Xuan enshrined there.

sentences.zh: 如此，則僖祖自居別廟之尊，三祖不祔子孫之廟。

translations.literal: In this way Emperor Xi would hold the dignity of a separate temple while the three ancestors would not be enshrined in descendants' temples.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Emperor Xi would hold separate-temple dignity while the three ancestors would not be enshrined in descendants' temples.

sentences.zh: 自漢、魏以來，太祖而 上，毀廟之主皆不合食，今遇祫，則即廟而享，於禮尤稱。」

translations.literal: Since Han and Wei, tablets of ancestors above Taizu whose temples were dismantled have not shared the feast; now at the xiá they would be honored at their own temple—this is especially fitting in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei, dismantled ancestors above Taizu have not shared the feast; now at the xiá they would be honored at their own temple—especially fitting.

sentences.zh: 諸儒如樓鑰、陳傅良皆以為可，詔從之。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars such as Lou Yue and Chen Fuliang all considered this acceptable, and an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars Lou Yue and Chen Fuliang approved, and an edict followed.

sentences.zh: 時朱熹在講筵，獨入議狀，條其不可者四，大略 云：「準尚書吏部牒，集議四祖祧主宜有所歸。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Xi was at the lecture throne and alone submitted a deliberation listing four objections, in substance stating: "According to the Ministry of Personnel dispatch, deliberation is sought on where the four removed ancestral tablets should be placed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi, then at the lecture throne, alone submitted objections in four points, stating in substance: "According to the Ministry dispatch, deliberation is sought on where the four removed ancestral tablets should be placed.

sentences.zh: 今詳群議雖多，而皆有可疑。

translations.literal: Now though the many deliberations are numerous, all have doubtful points.
translations.idiomatic: Though deliberations are many, all have doubtful points.

sentences.zh: 若曰藏之夾室，則是以祖宗之主下藏於子孫之夾室。

translations.literal: If they are stored in the side chamber, then ancestors' tablets are stored below in descendants' side chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Storing them in the side chamber places ancestors' tablets below in descendants' side chambers.

sentences.zh: 至於祫祭，設幄於夾室之前，則亦 不得謂之祫。

translations.literal: When at the xiá sacrifice enclosures are set before the side chamber, it still cannot be called a xiá.
translations.idiomatic: Setting enclosures before the side chamber at the xiá still cannot be called a xiá.

sentences.zh: 欲別立一廟，則喪事即遠，有毀無立。

translations.literal: If a separate temple is built, the mourning is already remote and there is dismantling without establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Building a separate temple fails because mourning is remote—there is dismantling without establishment.

sentences.zh: 欲藏之天興殿，則宗廟、原廟不可相雜。

translations.literal: If they are stored in the Hall of Heavenly Prosperity, then the ancestral temple and the original temple must not be mixed.
translations.idiomatic: Storing them in the Hall of Heavenly Prosperity mixes ancestral and original temples improperly.

sentences.zh: 議者皆知其不安，特以其心欲尊奉太祖三年一袷時暫東向之故，其實無 益於太祖之尊，而徒使僖祖、太祖兩朝威靈，相與校強弱於冥冥之中。

translations.literal: Deliberators all know this is unsound, yet because they wish to honor Taizu by having him temporarily face east once every three years at the xiá, in fact this does not enhance Taizu's dignity but only sets the majesty of Emperors Xi and Taizu against each other in the unseen realm.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberators know this is unsound, yet wish Taizu to face east temporarily every three years—this does not enhance Taizu's dignity but sets Emperors Xi and Taizu against each other in the unseen realm.

sentences.zh: 今但以太祖當日追尊帝號之令而默推之，則知今日太祖在天之靈，必有所不忍而不敢當矣。

translations.literal: If one silently infers from the day Taizu was posthumously ennobled with an imperial title, then Taizu's spirit in Heaven today would surely be unable to bear and dare not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: Inferring from the day Taizu received his posthumous imperial title, his spirit in Heaven today would surely be unable to bear this.

sentences.zh: 又 況僖祖祧主遷於治平，不過數年，神宗復奉以為始祖，已為得禮之正而合於人心，所謂『有其舉之，莫敢廢者』。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Emperor Xi's tablet was removed in Zhiping, yet within a few years Shenzong again honored him as founding ancestor—this was already the correct ritual and accorded with human hearts; as the saying goes, 'When someone undertakes it, none dare abolish it.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xi's tablet was removed in Zhiping, yet Shenzong soon restored him as founding ancestor—already correct ritual accordant with hearts; 'when someone undertakes it, none dare abolish it.'

sentences.zh: 又言：「當以僖祖為始祖，如周之後稷，太祖如 周之文王，太宗如周之武王，與仁宗之廟，皆萬世不祧；

translations.literal: He further stated: "Emperor Xi should be taken as founding ancestor, like Hou Ji of Zhou; Taizu like King Wen of Zhou; Taizong like King Wu; together with Renzong's temple—all never to be removed;
translations.idiomatic: He further stated: "Emperor Xi should be founding ancestor like Zhou's Hou Ji; Taizu like King Wen; Taizong like King Wu; with Renzong's temple—all never removed;

sentences.zh: 昭穆而次，以至高宗之廟亦萬世不祧。」

translations.literal: the zhao and mu in sequence down to Gaozong's temple also never to be removed."
translations.idiomatic: zhao and mu in sequence down to Gaozong's temple also never removed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「元祐大儒程頤以為王安石言『僖祖不當祧』，復立廟為得 禮。

translations.literal: He further stated: "The great Ru scholar Cheng Yi of Yuanyou held that Wang Anshi's saying 'Emperor Xi ought not be removed' and restoring a temple was obtaining ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He further stated: "Great scholar Cheng Yi of Yuanyou held that Anshi's view that Emperor Xi ought not be removed and restoring a temple obtained ritual.

sentences.zh: 竊詳頤之議論與安石不同，至論此事則深服之，足以見義理人心之所同，固有不約而合者。
